stage1.impression: An armillary globe of six coloured rings with see-through 'acrylic' faces, leaning about 23.4° (Earth's tilt), next to a chunky EARF wordmark. On night it glows like stained glass, and the end lockup is balanced and held long enough. As a mark it is not there yet. On paper the overlaps go olive, grey and brown. The full-strength coloured rims make it read as a cage of hoops, not solid shapes. Hairline seams run through the fills. The rings poke past the ball, so the outline is lumpy. The black-only and white-only versions rely on grey tints that fill the centre solid, so it is not a true one-colour mark. The ident's idea (a gyro spinning down, tilting to Earth's axis, stepping aside for the name) is right, but it plays as separate moves. It opens at full spin, and the see-through rotation can be read turning either way. The tilt, the only beat that could only be EARF, is the weakest stretch on the trace. Motion dies to a dead stop at about 1.7-2.0 s, restarts with a jolt, and the move aside ends in a hard stop. The name then arrives as four one-frame typewriter pops (2.57-2.77 s) before a still hold. A competent draft, not yet the brand's own.

keep: The material idea: the discs as tinted cast acrylic, the cabinets' own material, laid front to back so the nearest face leads. On ink it already glows like stained glass. Keep this layering model; only its weights and mixing change below.

The gyro arc and the lockup: a spin on its axis that settles at Earth's 23.4° and steps aside for EARF, ending on a balanced lockup (globe about 1.4x the cap height, centred on the caps, even side margins) held about 1.3 s.

changes.problem: The faces are so thin that the globe reads as a pale bubble behind a cage of hoops, not as the discs made transparent, which is the owner's 'it looks very different'.
changes.evidence: Sheet 1, 'acrylic: multicolour' beside 'discs: multicolour': the acrylic ball is a washed sage, and inside it the crossings mix down to greys and khakis. Measured on the tiles, the median OKLCh chroma is 0.065 against 0.113 for the discs, and 26 % of the ball is near-grey against 1.4 %. On ink (sheet 2, frames 01-07) the ball is murky olive, and the near and far halves of each disc are almost equally strong, so the spin in frames 01-04 (0.00-1.13 s) can be read turning either way.
changes.expected: Each disc's own colour comes first, and the discs' layout (orange and violet lens, blue wedges, red and yellow caps on a green ball) reads at a glance. Far halves show as ghosts at about a fifth of their colour on paper. On ink the ball becomes a lit green instead of olive. In frames 01-04 the nearest faces dominate, so the turn reads one way. Simulated with the card's model: mean OKLab distance to the discs falls from 0.061 to 0.038 with this change alone. Apply it together with change 3, or the one-colour rails fill in solid.

accept.at: sheet 1, acrylic: multicolour and multicolour on ink
accept.check: Next to the discs tiles, does each acrylic tile show the same pattern of colour areas, each in its own colour, with the far halves only as faint see-through ghosts?

changes.problem: The full-strength coloured edges outline every disc, so in colour the acrylic reads as the lines style with tinted fills, a stroked look the owner ruled out for the colour discs.
changes.evidence: Sheet 1, 'acrylic: multicolour' and 'multicolour on ink': the six coloured rims (0.045 of the radius) are the strongest marks in the tile, and the eye reads hoops, not discs. Sheet 2, frames 01-06 (0.00-1.87 s): the orange and violet rims are the brightest lines in the frame. In frames 09-12 (2.97-4.10 s), at lockup size, the rims are most of what is seen of the small globe.
changes.expected: Colour areas meet edge to edge, as in the discs tile, with no ring drawn. The acrylic now reads through its faces: ghosted far halves and mixed crossings. Applies to the multicolour rails and the ident; change 3 sets the one-colour rails. Simulated with change 1, distance to the discs falls further, from 0.038 to 0.028.

accept.check: Do the colour areas meet edge to edge, with no coloured outline drawn round any disc?

changes.problem: In one colour the acrylic relies on grey tints that stack to solid in the centre, so it is not a true one-colour mark and the rings vanish where the eye looks; change 1 would turn it into a solid blob.
changes.evidence: Sheet 1, 'acrylic: black only': the centre of the ball is a flat #302D2B with no ring visible across a 30 px square, and the only contrast left is grey slivers at the rim. 'White only' is the same in reverse (flat #EDECE9). Neither can be printed in one solid ink, foiled or laser-etched on a cabinet without halftones. Simulated at face 0.72 and edge 0, the black-only tile becomes a near-solid blob.
changes.from: faces as tints of the one colour (face 0.45 on paper, 0.55 on ink) plus edges at 0.045 of the radius

to.edge_halves: near and far, both solid in the rail's colour

changes.expected: The three non-colour tiles look like the lines tiles: a clean ring globe in one solid colour, printable in a single ink. This matches the owner's rule that the strokes are the non-colour versions, and stays clean however far change 1 raises the faces.

accept.at: sheet 1, acrylic: black only, white only, one colour
accept.check: Is each tile drawn in one solid colour on its ground, rings only, with no grey or tinted area anywhere?

changes.problem: 'Over' averages colours in sRGB, so crossings drift to grey, khaki and brown instead of clean new colours, the opposite of the owner's 'crossing primary colors created secondary colors'.
changes.evidence: Sheet 1, 'acrylic: multicolour': the central lens, where the orange, violet, blue and green faces cross, is grey-mauve and grey-orange. The far half of the red disc seen through the green is brown. 26 % of the ball has OKLCh chroma under 0.05. Simulated: even at face 0.72, sRGB 'over' leaves about 5 % of the ball near-grey and the median chroma at only 0.082.
changes.expected: Crossings become clear new colours: red over yellow gives orange, yellow and blue give green, blue over red gives violet, and blue seen through green gives teal. No grey or brown patch is left. Simulated: median chroma 0.121 against 0.129 for the discs, near-grey area 1.7 %, distance to the discs 0.023. For print and vector files, each crossing is exported as a flat colour computed by this rule, not as live transparency.

accept.check: Is every crossing inside the ball a clear, saturated colour (teal, orange, violet, olive), with no grey, khaki or brown patch?

changes.problem: The faces are built from pieces whose shared edges show as hairlines, so the acrylic looks cracked rather than cast.
changes.evidence: Sheet 1, 'acrylic: multicolour' at 3-4x zoom: pale dotted lines run straight out from the centre across areas of even colour, for example the brown-orange area left of centre. A per-pixel render of the same model shows none, so they come from how the faces are built. In the ident they would crawl over the faces as the globe spins (frames 01-07, 0.00-2.23 s).
changes.from: faces drawn as split pieces whose shared edges are antialiased separately

to.faces: one filled path per visible region (union of its pieces), or per-pixel compositing
allowed_boundaries: the straight crossing lines where the depth order flips

changes.expected: No hairline inside any area of even colour at any zoom, on paper or on ink. During the spin the faces stay clean, and the only boundaries are real ones.

accept.check: Is every area of even colour free of thin pale or dark lines?

changes.problem: The ident dies midway, with a dead stop after the tilt and a jolting restart into the move aside, which itself ends in a hard stop, so it plays as separate moves rather than one gesture.
changes.evidence: Sheet 2 trace (y scale from the letter pops, whose peaks match each letter's area): the tilt's hump fades to zero at about 1.71 s ('whole'). The change stays under 0.2 % from about 1.64 to 2.05 s (about 0.4 s), and frame 06 (t = 1.87 s) falls in this dead stretch. Then the trace jumps from 0 to about 1.1 % of the picture in three frames (2.02-2.10 s, 'aside'). It is still at about 0.5 % at 2.50 s and drops to zero the next frame.

from.end: stops from about 0.5 % in one frame

changes.expected: No dead beat: the globe finishes its tilt while already gliding aside, so frame 06 (t = 1.87 s) shows it smaller and left of centre. The trace makes one rounded hump from the tilt's tail through the aside, with no flat floor at 1.64-2.05 s and no cliff at 2.02 s. The globe slows to rest at 2.35 s instead of stopping from about 0.5 %.

changes.problem: The name arrives as four one-frame typewriter pops, the harshest changes in the ident and a generic device unrelated to the globe.
changes.evidence: Sheet 2 trace: four isolated spikes at 2.57, 2.63, 2.70 and 2.77 s, each a single frame changing 1.6-2.2 % of the picture (each equals one letter's area, so each letter cuts on whole), with a still frame between them. They are the tallest peaks in the ident. Frame 08 (t = 2.60 s) shows the parked globe with a lone 'E'.
changes.from: E, A, R, F each cut on whole in one frame at 2.57, 2.63, 2.70, 2.77 s

to.letters: still at final positions, full opacity

changes.expected: The name is drawn out of the globe's rim as the globe comes to rest. Frame 07 (t = 2.23 s) shows the wordmark part-revealed, and frame 08 (t = 2.60 s) the full lockup. On the trace, the four spikes give way to one smooth falling tail ending by 2.60 s, and the hold grows to about 1.5 s (2.60-4.13 s).

accept.check: Is the wordmark only partly revealed, cut off by a clean vertical edge, with the letters to its right not yet shown?

changes.problem: The tilt to 23.4°, the one move that could only be EARF, is the weakest moment on the trace and reads as drift.
changes.evidence: Sheet 2 trace between 'tilt' (1.13 s) and 'whole' (1.71 s): a low hump peaking at about 0.5 % of the picture at 1.40 s, a third of the opening spin (about 1.4 % at 0.00 s) and of the aside (about 1.9 % at 2.22 s). The hand-off from the spin dips to about 0.2 % at 1.11-1.17 s. Frames 04-06 (1.13-1.87 s) show the lean simply arriving, with no accent.
changes.expected: The globe leans past its tilt and settles into it, like a gyroscope finding Earth's axis, overlapping the start of the aside. Frame 05 (t = 1.50 s) shows the over-lean. The trace peaks at about 0.8-1.0 % in 1.1-1.5 s, with no dip at the hand-off from the spin.

accept.check: Does the equator lean visibly further than in frame 12 (about 26° against 23.4°)?

most_important: Change 1: raise face to 0.72 on paper and 0.80 on ink. On its own it moves the acrylic most of the way from a pale cage of hoops to the discs made transparent, which is what the owner asked for (simulated distance to the discs 0.061 to 0.038). Make change 3 with it so the one-colour rails do not fill in solid.
out_of_scope: The lumpy outline (the north and south discs and the side meridians poke past the green disc at the top right and bottom left) costs memorability and small-size clarity. It comes from the fixed geometry, and the discs have it too. Rounding it off with an outline or a ball tint would make the acrylic differ from the discs, and an outline is a stroke the owner ruled out.

The owner's wish that crossing primaries make secondaries can only show literally in thin slivers. Red, blue and yellow are the three parallels, so in the fixed geometry they overlap only where the north and south discs graze the equator in projection; most crossings are with the green ball and the orange and violet meridians. Change 4 makes every crossing a clean colour, but large orange, green and violet areas from primaries crossing are not possible in this geometry.

The colour pairs opposite each other on the wheel (orange with blue, red with green, violet with yellow) cross in the centre of the ball and will always be the weakest mixes in any model. The six colours are fixed.
The discs and lines styles are fixed. Change 3 reuses the lines stroke weight (0.075 of the radius) for the acrylic's non-colour rails without changing the lines style.
for_owner: Which acrylic do you mean? We recommend the bright look where the nearest face shows most and crossings are mixed clean (changes 1 and 4). The other choice is a true filter look (multiply), which is how real tinted acrylic mixes, but with four discs stacked at the centre the core goes near-black (simulated even at today's face 0.45).

Should the acrylic hand its black-only, white-only and one-colour versions to strokes at the lines weight (change 3, your own rule for the discs)? Or should it keep a one-colour form of its own: near edges 0.075 and far edges 0.035 of the radius, which reads as see-through in one ink?
Do you want a cut-edge glint in colour (each disc's edge at about 0.012 of the radius in its own colour)? It adds an acrylic cue, but it is a stroke, which you ruled out for the discs.
Changes 6-8 re-time the gyro ident. If the same choreography serves the discs and lines idents, approve it for all styles so they stay one system.
